procedure.description: application of skin substitute graft to the foot, first 25 square centimeters, diabetic foot ulcer

denial.carcText: Payment adjusted because the payer deems the information submitted does not support this many/frequency of services.
denial.text: Copperfield Health denied the claim for CPT 15271 (application of skin substitute graft to the foot, first 25 square centimeters, diabetic foot ulcer) with date of service 2026-02-17. CARC 151: Payment adjusted because the payer deems the information submitted does not support this many/frequency of services. RARC N10: Adjustment based on the findings of a review organization. Payer remark: The number of applications billed exceeds what the documentation supports for this wound.

criteria.text: Full-thickness diabetic foot ulcer, Wagner grade 1 or 2, present for at least 4 weeks, without exposed bone or tendon, active infection, or osteomyelitis.

At least 4 weeks of standard wound care with documented serial measurements showing less than 50 percent reduction in wound area: sharp debridement, offloading, moist wound dressings, infection control, and glycemic management.
Adequate arterial perfusion documented: ankle-brachial index of 0.7 or greater, toe pressure of 40 mmHg or greater, or transcutaneous oxygen pressure of 30 mmHg or greater.
Hemoglobin A1c of 12 percent or less, an offloading device in place, and tobacco cessation counseling where applicable.

chart.text: Vitamin D came back 24. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.

Called his with the cholesterol results. Total 215, LDL 120, HDL 52, triglycerides 109. Discussed diet and walking. He wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
He called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the spring. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 13 and 13. No ocular pathology noted.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 5 years.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 2.8, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 75. Repeat in a year.
Work note requested for a sick day last Thursday. Faxed to the employer.

Here with a cough and congestion for 6 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if he gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Patient called about a tick bite on the scalp after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.

Mole on the right calf that his spouse noticed. About 6 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change he is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 5 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.

65 year old man with type 2 diabetes for 20 years and peripheral neuropathy, new to the wound center, referred by podiatry. Did not notice the ulcer until his daughter saw blood on the sock. His history otherwise: osteoarthritis of the hands. Allergies: codeine makes him sick. Never smoked, occasional beer, has three kids at home. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Plantar right forefoot ulcer under the first metatarsal head, present 9 weeks, 3.3 by 2.1 centimeters and 0.3 deep, full thickness into subcutaneous tissue, does not probe to bone, no exposed tendon, Wagner grade 2. No cellulitis, no drainage, no odor. Offloading boot dispensed today, fitted, he agrees to wear it for all weight bearing. Nonsmoker.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Hemoglobin A1c 7.8 percent. Creatinine 1.5. Albumin 3.8.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Right foot three views: no osteomyelitis, no soft tissue gas, no foreign body. Neuropathic changes at the midfoot.
Week 1 of standard care. Sharp debridement to healthy bleeding tissue, collagen dressing, offloading boot worn per patient. 3.3 by 2.1.
Arterial studies. Ankle-brachial index right 0.99, left 1.00, triphasic waveforms, right toe pressure 61 mmHg. Adequate perfusion for healing.
Blood pressure check. 137 over 88 today, 144 over 76 on repeat. He has been taking the lisinopril 10 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 8 weeks.
Week 2. Sharp debridement, collagen dressing. 3.2 by 2.1. Boot compliance good.
Week 3. Sharp debridement, collagen dressing. 3.1 by 2.0. Slow.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, he will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

Week 4. 3.1 by 2.0, area 6.2 square centimeters, down from 6.9 at the start, about 10 percent reduction after 4 weeks of standard care with debridement, offloading, and moist dressings. Less than 50 percent; qualifies for a cellular tissue product. Sharp debridement today.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.

Application of a cellular tissue-based product to the right plantar forefoot ulcer after sharp debridement, 4 square centimeters, secured with a nonadherent dressing and the offloading boot. Weekly follow-up.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 151 denial can be answered from the record.
